Flag the first row of each group

Source: R/is_first.R
is_first.Rd

is_first() is TRUE for the first row of each distinct combination of its arguments and FALSE for the others, like Stata's egen t = tag(id year). Use it in dplyr::mutate() or dplyr::filter(), for example to count or summarise each group once.

Usage

is_first(..., .missing = FALSE)

Arguments

...

Vectors of equal length that define the groups. Omit them in grouped dplyr::mutate() (or with .by) to flag the first row of each group.

.missing

If FALSE (default), rows with a missing value in any explicitly supplied argument are FALSE, as Stata's tag() does without its missing option. If TRUE, missing values form groups of their own. With no arguments, flag the first row of every current data-mask group, including groups with missing keys, regardless of .missing.

Value

A logical vector with one value per input row, or per row in the current data-mask group when no arguments are supplied.

Details

"First" follows the current row order. Unlike duplicates_tag(), which counts the other rows sharing the same values, is_first() marks one row per group. Missing values include tagged and SPSS user-missing values.

See also

Other data checking functions: assert(), keys, stata_merge()

Examples

panel <- tibble::tibble(
  id = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 2, NA),
  year = c(2001, 2002, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2001)
)
dplyr::mutate(panel, first = is_first(id))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>      id  year first
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <lgl>
#> 1     1  2001 TRUE 
#> 2     1  2002 FALSE
#> 3     2  2001 TRUE 
#> 4     2  2002 FALSE
#> 5     2  2003 FALSE
#> 6    NA  2001 FALSE

# Including the missing group
dplyr::mutate(panel, first = is_first(id, .missing = TRUE))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>      id  year first
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <lgl>
#> 1     1  2001 TRUE 
#> 2     1  2002 FALSE
#> 3     2  2001 TRUE 
#> 4     2  2002 FALSE
#> 5     2  2003 FALSE
#> 6    NA  2001 TRUE 

# The no-argument shortcut also includes the missing id group
dplyr::mutate(panel, first = is_first(), .by = id)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>      id  year first
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <lgl>
#> 1     1  2001 TRUE 
#> 2     1  2002 FALSE
#> 3     2  2001 TRUE 
#> 4     2  2002 FALSE
#> 5     2  2003 FALSE
#> 6    NA  2001 TRUE 

# Count panels
is_first(panel$id) |> sum()
#> [1] 2
